chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the one in Ihram who killed a louse?' He said: 'There is nothing upon him regarding the lice, and it is not befitting that he deliberately kills it.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing lice while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that killing a louse while in Ihram incurs no fidyah (expiation), distinguishing it from other insects that require compensation. The phrase 'la yanbaghi an yata’ammada' indicates that while not sinful, one should avoid deliberate, forceful killing, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease and minimal burden in ritual purity laws. This hadith is foundational in the chapter on Ihram regulations, illustrating the nuanced approach to minor impurities during sacred states.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘What are youasws saying regarding the one in Ihraam having killed the lice?’ Heasws said: ‘There is nothing upon him regarding the lice, and it is not befitting that he deliberately kills it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘ Ammar who has said

the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who in the state of Ihram kills a louse. He (the Imam) said, ‘There is nothing on him for it, but it is not proper to do so knowingly.’”
